facts.statement: No universal default passwords — each device or account must ship with a password unique per unit, or require the user to set their own credentials before first use.
facts.source_title: Most Important Parts of ETSI EN 303 645 Standard

facts.statement: The product must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy and support timely software/firmware updates.
facts.source_title: Most Important Parts of ETSI EN 303 645 Standard

facts.statement: Under California SB-327 (for any device sold in California), if a device can be authenticated from outside the local network, it must use a preprogrammed password unique to each device, or require the user to generate new credentials on first access.
facts.source_title: Understanding the California IoT Security Law (SB-327)

facts.statement: Commands to safety-critical devices (door locks, cameras) must be encrypted in transit and mutually authenticated between app and device.
facts.source_title: Understanding the California IoT Security Law (SB-327)

facts.statement: Device control should support the Matter interoperability standard, so a device can be registered with multiple controllers/ecosystems (multi-admin) rather than being locked to one proprietary hub.
facts.source_title: Matter & Thread: Smart Home Interoperability in 2026

facts.statement: Location- and occupancy-derived data (from automation routines and energy insights) must be collected under informed consent with data minimisation, consistent with GDPR/CCPA-style requirements.
